clue.text: Old monk's room in French church? Goodness!

parts.note: ex- means former or old
a monk sleeps in a cell
en is the French for in
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the sight of an old monk's quarters in a French church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodness!' looks like a mere exclamation, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellence is outstanding quality or merit, a synonym of goodness.

clue.text: Enjoyment found in Eastbourne as ever

indicators.note: the letters are found within the run of words Eastbourne as ever

explanation.surface: A seaside town in Sussex offers the same pleasure it always has.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is comfort and relaxed pleasure, close in sense to enjoyment.

clue.text: Clean home wrecked for changeable type

indicators.note: wrecked means the letters of clean home are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A fickle person makes a mess of a tidy house.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon is figuratively a person who keeps altering opinions or appearance, like the colour-shifting lizard.

clue.text: Catch young female duck

parts.note: a lass is a girl
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so O

explanation.surface: An instruction to grab a girl's duck.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso is to capture an animal with a noosed rope, a verb for catching.

clue.text: When muddled, say sect offers exalted feeling

indicators.note: muddled means the letters of say sect are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A confused religious sect is said to provide spiritual rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is an overwhelming state of joy or rapture.

clue.text: Firm at it trapping lake bird

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: trapping means the words at it hold a letter inside them

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A company busy at work catches a bird by a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The coal tit is a small European songbird of the titmouse family.

clue.text: Family departs? Gracious!

parts.note: kin are one's relatives
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise that the family is leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gracious!' reads as an exclamation but is the adjective being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Gracious and kind are synonyms, both meaning courteous and benevolent.

clue.text: Current understanding gives example

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
a deal is an agreement or understanding

explanation.surface: A present-day agreement sets a precedent.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a model or standard to follow, an example of perfection.

clue.text: Florentine poet embracing one Latvian dabbler

indicators.note: embracing means the poet's name wraps round the other letters

parts.note: Dante Alighieri was born in Florence
I is the Roman numeral one
a Lett is a person from Latvia

explanation.surface: Dante hugs a man from Latvia who merely dabbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante takes up an art or subject superficially, an amateur dabbler.

clue.text: Jailbird pre-irons pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters of pre-irons are a poor arrangement to be fixed

explanation.surface: A convict irons his trousers in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers, but here it is slang for bad, signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A jailbird is an informal word for someone locked up in jail.

clue.text: Sailor boarding ship? Great balls of fire!

indicators.note: boarding means the sailor gets inside the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman climbs aboard and someone exclaims a famous oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great balls of fire!' sounds like an exclamation (and a rock song), but stars really are great balls of burning gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars are huge glowing spheres of plasma, a playful literal description.

clue.text: Criminal will rest, carrying a flight case?

indicators.note: carrying means the rearranged letters hold the a inside
criminal means the letters of will rest are crooked, rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook will relax while carrying a travel bag.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of WILL REST gives STIRWELL, which holds A. A flight case is luggage, but here the 'flight' is of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairwell is the vertical shaft that encases a flight of stairs.

clue.text: Booming English lad in verbal onslaught

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the rant

parts.note: a rant is a loud, angry tirade
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: An English boy is caught up in a furious tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonant describes a deep, reverberating sound, the same as a loud booming one.

clue.text: Port cracked open?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., the Croatian port on the Adriatic

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a burst bottle of port wine, but the port is a Croatian seaport.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the Dalmatian coastal city and also means burst or divided along a line.

clue.text: Rib served with a cake for urchin

parts.note: to rib or rag someone is to tease them
a muffin is a small cake

explanation.surface: Someone is teased and handed a cake meant for a street child.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a scruffy, ragged child, a synonym of urchin.

clue.text: Service people with it inside a year

indicators.note: inside means these letters sit within a and the year letter

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: People who are with it cram a service into a year.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenity is a useful facility or service, such as a library or swimming pool.

clue.text: How bright idea may arrive?

parts.note: a sudden brilliant thought comes suddenly, and bright suggests a burst of light

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bright' plays on light: a sudden inspiration arrives instantly, like a burst of light.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means instantly, the way inspiration strikes without warning.

clue.text: Inuits troubled by a hot country

indicators.note: troubled means the letters of Inuits are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Arctic people are distressed by a sweltering nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a North African nation with a famously warm climate.

clue.text: Persist: what scrap metal dealer did around Spain?

indicators.note: around means the phrase goes round the Spain letter

parts.note: a scrap merchant sold iron
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A question asks what a scrap dealer did in Spain while urging perseverance.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is an idiom for carrying on doggedly despite difficulty.

clue.text: Knight in Scottish town also writer

indicators.note: in means the knight letter goes inside the town

parts.note: Ayr is a town on the Ayrshire coast of Scotland
N is the chess notation for knight
and means also

explanation.surface: A knight in a Scottish town is also an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayn Rand was a Russian-American novelist, author of The Fountainhead.

clue.text: Rescue ship

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to ship goods is to send or ... them

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a lifeboat, but ship is a verb for sending goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both setting free from danger and transporting goods to a recipient.

clue.text: Metal band RC allowed on Channel Islands

indicators.note: on means the letters follow after the island abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written: RC stands for Roman Catholic
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A Roman Catholic group of musicians is permitted to play on Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Metal band' suggests heavy rock musicians, but it is a ring of metal; the Channel Islands lie between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: A circlet is a small circular ornamental band, such as a metal headband.

clue.text: V-sign from revolutionary facing Reagan?

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine-Cuban revolutionary
V stands for versus, against or facing
Ron was the first name of US president Reagan

explanation.surface: A rude gesture from a revolutionary confronting an American president.
explanation.walkthrough: A V-sign is a rude hand gesture in Britain, but here it is literally a V-shaped sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is a V-shaped stripe or mark, as on a uniform sleeve or road sign.

clue.text: Routine America oddly unable to follow

indicators.note: to follow means these letters come after the America letters

parts.note: US is short for United States, America

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of unable

explanation.surface: An American routine that the nation cannot keep up with.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual and routine are synonyms for normal or habitual.

clue.text: Article dropped by dirty pawnbroker

indicators.note: dropped by means the article is removed from the word for dirty

parts.note: unclean means dirty
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grubby pawnbroker drops an item.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle is old British slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle is an informal old term for a pawnbroker, as in 'my watch is at my uncle's'.

clue.text: See 28
Appreciate Juliet in that role finally reversed

indicators.note: reversed means the whole assembled string is read backwards
in means the Juliet letter goes inside

parts.note: yon is an old word for that
J is Juliet in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of role

explanation.surface: Praising an actress playing Juliet, whose part ends up turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: YON plus E (the end of 'role') is YONE; J goes in to give YOJNE, which 'reversed' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To enjoy something is to take pleasure in it, to appreciate it.

clue.text: Bag from fringes of Carnaby Street

indicators.note: fringes of takes the first and last letters of Carnaby and of Street

explanation.surface: A handbag bought on the edges of a famous London shopping street.
explanation.walkthrough: Carnaby Street is a London shopping street; a cyst is a sac, so 'bag' is the medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is a closed sac in the body filled with fluid, a bag in the anatomical sense.

clue.text: Preserve dignity with this female: brilliant goalie?

parts.note: ace means excellent, brilliant
a goalkeeper is someone who saves shots

explanation.surface: A woman keeps her pride by being an excellent goalkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A face-saver is an action that lets someone avoid humiliation and keep their reputation.

clue.text: Eccentric Rye jeweller is rock and roller

indicators.note: eccentric means the letters of Rye jeweller is are oddly rearranged

explanation.surface: A quirky jeweller from the Sussex town of Rye is a rock musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerry Lee Lewis was a pioneering American rock and roll pianist and singer.

clue.text: Christmas — without the Spanish?

parts.note: no means without, as in no money
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A question whether Christmas would be the same without Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a word for Christmas, from the French Noël, used in carols.

clue.text: Relative difficulty in loosening tie?

parts.note: a granny is a grandmother, a relative
a knot is a tangled problem or difficulty

explanation.surface: A family member struggles to undo a tie.
explanation.walkthrough: A granny knot is a badly tied reef knot that slips, so it is a tie that tends to work loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A granny knot is a faulty double knot notorious for slipping undone.
